short_answer: Bryan Power is an active pick seller on WagerTalk, a Las Vegas marketplace founded in July 2015 with written terms and a refund policy. His WagerTalk page has existed since at least July 2022, when his bio said he was arriving "as hot as ever." He also appears on WagerTalk's video and podcast shows. The page was updated on 17 Nov 2026 and sells single plays, short passes and a one year pass.

Whether the picks make money over time is not shown in any full record we could open. The page leads with "NOW UP 93.1 UNITS ~ IN ALL SPORTS ~ SINCE APRIL!" and "24-10 (70%) RUN WITH ALL FOOTBALL!", streaks that start where the seller chose. The Last 20 table on the same page showed 9 wins and 11 losses, about 3.5 units down at one unit a play, and its 16 football plays went 8 and 8. The site's own 30 day leaderboard, by contrast, had him at 33 wins, 22 losses and 2 pushes.

We found very few independent posts about him. The few we found were neutral or mildly positive, and none came from a paying customer describing results. Treat him as an established but unproven seller and record every pick yourself.
pricing_intro: All prices below were on the Bryan Power WagerTalk page on 17 Nov 2026. WagerTalk shows a higher list price next to most sale prices; we give both. The All Access passes on the page are sold from his page and the 3 and 7 day passes said "Currently 1 Pick(s) Included!", so check how many plays a pass will actually cover before buying. In July 2022 the same page sold a 3 Day Pass for $59 and NFL plus CFB through the Super Bowl for $899.

guarantee: The guarantee is an extra you pay for. A $5.00 play costs $8.00 with it. WagerTalk says the option "backs your purchase with 100% in credits." The refund policy explains: "If your daily pick(s) package does not result in an overall profit across all included plays, the paid cash value of a guaranteed pick will be credited back to your account to be used on a future purchase." The paid amount comes back as account credit, not as cash.

The WagerTalk refund policy also says "All Sales are Final and products are sold "as is"" and "Once a product or service has been purchased, delivered, and/ or viewed, no refunds will be issued." The site terms say the content is "for entertainment and amusement purposes only" and that "the purchaser's exclusive remedy, shall be a refund of the price paid" or replacement of the product, at WagerTalk's option. Losses on the bets themselves are never covered.

claims_note: Two numbers on the same site pull in different directions. The leaderboard showed him 33 and 22 and 2 over the last 30 days, while the Last 20 table on his own page was 9 and 11 and ran from 4 to 16 Nov 2026. Both can be true at once: his best weeks were earlier in the month and his latest 20 plays were worse. That is exactly why a buyer needs the full list, not the best window.

The bio has changed over time. In July 2022 it said he "held the #1 all-time ranking inside the Octagon at SportsCapping" for UFC; the 2026 version says he spent "the previous decade at Covers Experts." We could not open an old profile on either site to check his results there.
Each streak starts on a date the seller chose, and the dollar figures assume a stake the page does not explain.
record: Watchdog graded sample, new 22 Nov 2026. Bryan Power does not publish a complete, time stamped log we can audit, so we built a sample from public posts that carry their plays. Watchdog captures X accounts and forum threads that post or repost picks; the ones naming Bryan Power most often were WagerTalkPicks, TheGodOfCappers, 1218Sports, EZMSports. From 22 Sep 2026 to 14 Nov 2026 we took every play our parser could read inside a Bryan Power block, kept only those posted before the game started, removed repeats, and graded each one against the final score at one unit risked, at the odds shown or -110 when none were shown.

Result: 6 plays, 3 won, 3 lost, -0.24 units, a return of -4.0% per unit risked. By sport: NCAAF 1 won, 3 lost, -2.06 units. By month: September 1 won, 0 lost, +0.91 units; October 1 won, 1 lost, -0.09 units; November 1 won, 2 lost, -1.06 units.
What it means: 6 decided plays is far too few to judge.
What a buyer can verify independently: no full, time stamped log of every paid pick that we could find.

What the seller publishes: streak totals, leaderboard entries such as 33 and 22 and 2 over the last 30 days, and a Last 20 table with odds. On 17 Nov 2026 the Last 20 table had 9 wins and 11 losses, including two six point teasers that won and a three team parlay that lost. At one unit a play and the listed odds, that comes to about minus 3.5 units. WagerTalk grades these itself and also sells the picks.

A third party: GameAdvisers, a site that says it may earn sportsbook commissions, tracks his free WagerTalk picks. On 17 Nov 2026 it showed 9 and 6 and plus $246 over the last 30 days, while another box on the same page said 9 and 7. That covers free picks only, a sample of about 15 plays, and the profit figures assume a flat $100 bet.

our_data.context: For scale: the streaks on his page run from about 60% to 82% winners, while his Last 20 table showed 45%.

customers_intro: Independent buyer evidence on Bryan Power is thin.

customers.text: We found only a few independent posts about Bryan Power: a 2013 Sportsbook Review tally of free picks that put him on top of a small group at 12 wins and 5 losses, and 2026 TheRX threads where WagerTalk sellers are on the list of services members may not post. No buyer complaint, and no detailed buyer praise of his paid packages, turned up in our searches across Reddit, TheRX, Covers and Sportsbook Review. Apart from WagerTalk's own numbers, the only tracking we found covers his free picks.

In an SBR thread comparing handicappers' free picks from early February to late March 2013, one member who kept a tally said Bryan Power was the best of the group at 12 wins and 5 losses, up 5.6 units. Others in the same tally were below even. That covered free picks only, not paid packages.

TheRX lists "All Wagertalk Cappers" among the services members may not post in its daily service play threads, and the rule was repeated on 14 Nov 2026. So his paid plays are rarely shared and checked there. We found no buyer post on TheRX describing his results.

Web searches found no Covers, SBR or TheRX thread reviewing his paid packages, no Trustpilot or Better Business Bureau page and no court or regulator record. The Reddit archive search of r/sportsbetting returned 6 posts, none about him; searches of r/sportsbook timed out, and our saved Reddit archive had no post naming him.

conflicts: WagerTalk sells his picks, grades his record, writes his bio and runs the leaderboard that ranks him. None of those numbers is independent of the seller.
WagerTalk also produces the video and podcast shows where he gives picks, so the publicity and the sales come from the same company.
GameAdvisers, the only outside tracker we found, describes him as part of the WagerTalk Group and carries an affiliate disclosure for sportsbook partners.
TheRX lists "All Wagertalk Cappers" among the services members may not post in its daily service play threads. The rule does not say why, and it says nothing about the quality of the picks.
strengths: Sold through a marketplace with a named Las Vegas seller address, written terms and a refund policy.
Prices are published for every play and pass, and single plays were on sale for $5.
The page shows a Last 20 table with odds and losses as well as wins, and on 17 Nov 2026 it was a losing stretch that the page did not hide.
His free picks are tracked by an outside site, and an old forum tally from 2013 had his free picks ahead of the group.
He has a long public history: an archived WagerTalk page from 2022 and a forum mention from 2013.
concerns: No full public record of paid picks. Every headline number is a streak chosen by the seller.
His own Last 20 table was 9 and 11, and its football plays were 8 and 8, against a headline "24-10" football run.
The guarantee costs extra and pays in site credit, never cash. All sales are final.
Some bio numbers are years old, such as the "this year (2022)" run, and the bio has described his past differently over time.
Very few independent buyer posts exist, good or bad.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Open the Last 20 tab before you buy. On the day we checked it told a different story from the streak banners.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money, and parlays and teasers change the math.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Here it is credit only.
Check how many plays a pass includes; the short passes said "Currently 1 Pick(s) Included!"
faq: He is a real, active seller on WagerTalk, a Las Vegas marketplace with written terms, and he has sold there since at least 2022. We could not verify that his paid picks win over time, because no full record is published, and we found no court or regulator action involving him.
What does the Watchdog sample of Bryan Power show?
We graded 6 of their plays that were posted publicly before the game started, 22 Sep 2026 to 14 Nov 2026: 3 won, 3 lost, -0.24 units at one unit each. That is too few plays to judge.
How much does Bryan Power cost?

On 17 Nov 2026 single plays were $5.00 ($8.00 with the guarantee), short passes were $49.00, and a one year all inclusive pass was $1,188.00. All access passes ran from $39.00 for a day to $1,999.00 for a year.
Does Bryan Power have a verified record?

No. The page shows streaks such as up 93.1 units since April, graded by WagerTalk, while his own Last 20 table was 9 and 11. An outside site tracks only his free picks, about 15 of them over the last 30 days.
Does the WagerTalk guarantee give my money back?
No. The guarantee costs extra and, if the package does not show a profit, returns the price as account credit for a future purchase. All sales are final and betting losses are never covered.
Where did Bryan Power sell picks before WagerTalk?

His current bio says he spent the previous decade at Covers Experts. His 2022 bio also cited a UFC ranking at SportsCapping. We could not open his old profiles on those sites to check his results there.

Plays are cheap at $5, but nothing shows the paid picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of plays. The guarantee only returns site credit, and your betting losses are never covered.
